spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the forbidden-header-name guard that governs the WebTransport headers option by building a real Request and reading back which composed headers survived — accepted, silently dropped, or thrown — rather than consulting a hard-coded list.

interactive.rationale: An editable header list re-runs the guard experiment; verified the default eight headers produced 3 sent / 4 dropped / 1 rejected with per-header security rationales.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises watching each header be accepted, dropped, or rejected via a real Request, which the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: The silent-drop trap ('code that assumes its Cookie header went out is never told') and the thrown malformed-name case are both first-class, with the friendlier-failure contrast drawn.

conformance.rationale: The suite's forbidden-names-are-dropped-by-the-request-guard and byte-string assertions are exactly this experiment; 5 pass / 2 fail on Chromium 141 with only the Chrome-154 members failing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): ran the experiment — host/cookie/origin dropped silently by the real request guard, one malformed name threw, three custom headers survived, tally and narration correct; console clean, screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and logs sent/dropped/rejected per run.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, tally as dl, captioned table, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled textarea, captioned table with scoped headers, aria-live detail, 44px button.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read).

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/webtransport-headers-and-responseheaders/handshake-anatomy/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). The guard experiment is genuinely empirical — the browser's own Request machinery decides each header's fate — and the default set teaches the two failure modes that matter: forbidden names vanishing silently versus malformed names throwing. Per-header security rationales are accurate. Console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; no mobile overflow; feature /conformance/ honestly ran 5 pass / 2 fail. Clears the bar.
